To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the binding of [(3)H]epibatadine and 5[(3)H]A-8538 to mouse brain is eliminated by deletion of either of the two nicotinic receptor genes, β2 and α4.

the binding of α-conotoxin MII, A-85380 and epibatidine to brain nAChRs is dependent on expression of the α4, α5, α6 and β3 subunits, and that the binding of A-85380 to brain nACHRs is dependent on the expression of the β2 but not the β4 subunit.

α7* nAChRs are the only nAChR subtype that binds α-bungarotoxins, that α4 and β2 are the only n AChR subunits required for 5A-85380 and [(125) I]epibatidines binding and that the β4 subunit is required for the expression of β4* n AChRs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of nicotinic cholinergic receptors (nAchRs), which are expressed in the mammalian central nervous system (CNS), and the identification of their physiological roles.
the characterization of the molecular and pharmacological properties of nicotinic receptors in the central nervous systems of wild-type and mutant mice.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development and plasticity of the nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nAChRs labeled by [(125)I]-A-85380, [(125) I]-epibatidine, and [(125) I] α-conotoxinMlll are α4β2, α4β2*, α3β4*, α6β4* and α6β2*.

α2* and α4* nAchR are expressed at high density in the hippocampus and cerebral cortex, α2*, α6* and α4*nAChR are expressed at moderate levels in the hippocampus, and β2*nAChR is expressed at low density in the cerebellar cortex.
α4* and α4β2* nAChRs are present in the mouse brain, that α6* and β2* nACHRs are expressed in most brain regions and that α7 nAChRs and α4β4* nAchRs are present in only a few brain regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nAChRs labeled by the four radioligands can be defined as: (1) α7*, (2) α4β2, (3) α4β4, (4) α4β3 and (5) α3β4.
[(125)I]-A-85380 labels α4β2 and α6β2 sites, [(125) I]α-bungaro toxin labels α7 sites, and [(125) I]-epibatidine labels α4β4 and α6β4 sites.

the binding of [(3H)]nicotine is a poor indicator of nAChRs in the brain, whereas [(125)I]-A-85380 is a very sensitive indicator of α4β2 nAChR and the binding of [(123)I]epitidine is a sensitive indicator of β4* nACHR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many nAChRs in the central nervous systems of mice.
the nomenclature of nAChRs is not as clear-cut as previously thought and that the binding of a particular ligand does not always correlate with a specific nAChR subtype.
a variety of ligand binding methods can be used to evaluate the effects of nAChRs gene deletion on the distribution and properties of nAChRS.
